# __2\. System Architecture and Design__

2\.1 Architectural Overview

Awwab \(Smart Namaz Companion\) is a cross\-platform Islamic mobile application built using the Flutter framework with the Dart programming language\. The application follows a layered, service\-oriented architecture that cleanly separates concerns into distinct tiers: the UI Layer, State Management Layer, Service Layer, and Data/Persistence Layer\. This design promotes maintainability, testability, and a clear data flow throughout the application\.

The application is designed to serve as an all\-in\-one digital companion for Muslims who wish to maintain their daily prayer routine\. It integrates real\-time prayer time calculations, step\-by\-step Salah guidance, a Qibla compass, a digital Tasbih counter, gamified streak tracking, Azan notification scheduling, a nearby mosque finder, and daily Hadith — all within a single, cohesive, and beautifully themed interface\. The name "Awwab" \(أَوَّاب\) is Arabic for "one who frequently returns to Allah," reflecting the app's mission to encourage consistent prayer habits\.

The application targets six platforms from a single Dart codebase: Android \(primary\), iOS, Web \(PWA\), macOS, Linux, and Windows\. The Flutter framework enables this true cross\-platform reach, allowing the team to maintain a unified codebase while delivering native\-quality experiences on each platform\.

2\.2 Layered Architecture

The application is organized into four primary layers, each with a well\-defined responsibility:

__Layer 1 — UI Layer \(Screens\)__

The topmost layer consists of Flutter screen widgets that render the user interface\. Each screen is implemented as a StatefulWidget and is responsible for presenting data to the user and capturing user interactions\. The app features eight main screens accessible through a bottom navigation bar and a side drawer: Home Screen \(Prayer Times\), Qibla Compass, Tasbeeh Counter, Reminders, Streak Tracker, Prayer Guidance, Mosque Map, and Settings\. Multiple custom CustomPainter classes are used throughout the app for rendering complex visuals such as the compass rose, tasbih beads, progress rings, and decorative wave patterns\.

__Layer 2 — State Management Layer \(Provider\)__

The application uses the Provider package for global state management\. Two providers are registered at the root: a LanguageProvider \(extending ChangeNotifier\) that manages the app\-wide language state, enabling instant switching between English and Urdu without restarting the app; and a ThemeNotifier \(also extending ChangeNotifier\) that manages the light/dark theme mode, persisting the user's preference to SharedPreferences\. Both are injected via MultiProvider in main\.dart and consumed throughout the widget tree using Consumer2\. Local screen\-level state \(such as counter values, selected prayers, and loading indicators\) is managed using standard Flutter StatefulWidget with setState\.

__Layer 3 — Service Layer__

The service layer contains stateless utility classes that encapsulate business logic, API communication, and device interactions\. Each service has a single responsibility: PrayerApiService handles HTTP communication with the Aladhan REST API; LocationService wraps the Geolocator plugin for GPS position retrieval; NotificationService manages local notification scheduling with a dual\-channel system \(system sound for prayer banners and custom Azan sound for manual reminders\); HadithService loads and parses the bundled Hadiths JSON asset; HijriService computes and formats today's Islamic calendar date; and StreakService manages the reading and writing of daily prayer completion records with an in\-memory cache for performance\.

__Layer 4 — Data/Persistence Layer__

The data layer handles persistent storage and data modeling\. All user preferences, notification toggles, theme/language settings, and streak records are stored locally using the SharedPreferences plugin \(key\-value storage\)\. Data models — PrayerTimeModel, HadithModel, and DailyPrayerRecord — provide structured representations of the app's domain objects with toJson\(\) and fromJson\(\) serialization methods\. The Hadith dataset is stored as a bundled JSON asset file \(assets/hadiths\.json\) loaded once at runtime\. Prayer times are also cached to SharedPreferences for instant display on app launch before fresh data is fetched from the API\. No external database or cloud service is required, ensuring full offline capability for stored data\.

2\.4 Navigation Architecture

Awwab employs two complementary navigation patterns:

__Bottom Navigation Bar \(Persistent Shell\):__

The MainWrapper widget serves as the persistent navigation shell, hosting a BottomNavigationBar with four primary tabs: Home \(Namaz/Prayer Times\) at index 0, Qibla Compass at index 1, Tasbeeh Counter at index 2, and Reminders at index 3\. An IndexedStack is used to keep all visited screens alive in the widget tree, preventing re\-initialization when switching tabs\. Tab labels are bilingual, switching between English and Urdu via the LanguageProvider\.

__Push Navigation \(Secondary Screens\):__

Secondary screens are navigated to using MaterialPageRoute and Navigator\.push, including: the Settings screen \(accessible from the side drawer and Reminders screen\), Prayer Guidance screen \(pushed when tapping a prayer time card on the Home screen\), Streak Tracker \(accessible from the Home screen\), and the Mosque Map screen\. The SplashScreen serves as the initial route, transitioning to the MainWrapper using a custom PageRouteBuilder with FadeTransition for a smooth cross\-fade animation\.

2\.5 State Management

The application employs the Provider package for managing app\-wide state\. Two global providers are registered at the root of the widget tree via MultiProvider:

• LanguageProvider: 

A ChangeNotifier that holds a language code \(defaulting to English\)\. When the user selects a language from the dropdown in Settings, the provider calls setLanguage\(\) followed by notifyListeners\(\), which triggers an immediate rebuild of all widgets that depend on the language state\. This enables instant, app\-wide language switching between English and Urdu without restarting the application\. Every user\-facing string in the app uses a ternary expression checking the isUrdu flag\.

ThemeNotifier: A ChangeNotifier that manages the light/dark theme preference\. It reads the initial theme mode from SharedPreferences on startup and persists changes when the user toggles the theme\. The toggleTheme\(\) and setSystemTheme\(\) methods update the ThemeMode and notify listeners, causing the entire MaterialApp to rebuild with the new theme\. Both providers are consumed by the root widget using Consumer2 for efficient rebuilds\.

Local screen\-level state — such as the Tasbih counter value, selected prayer for guidance, loading indicators, countdown timers, and form inputs — is managed using standard Flutter StatefulWidget with setState\. This keeps the state management simple and appropriate for the current scale of the application\.

2\.6 Service Layer

Each service is a stateless class with static or instance methods, encapsulating a single area of concern:

__Service__

__Responsibility__

PrayerApiService

Performs HTTP GET requests to the Aladhan API \(api\.aladhan\.com/v1/timings\) with GPS coordinates and ISNA calculation method; parses the JSON response into a PrayerTimeModel with a 10\-second timeout and graceful error handling\.

LocationService

Wraps the Geolocator plugin to fetch the device's current GPS latitude and longitude; handles permission denial gracefully with fallback error messages and retry options\.

NotificationService

Static utility class managing two notification channels: "azan\_channel" for prayer time banners with system sound, and "reminder\_azan\_channel" for manual reminders with custom Azan audio\. Uses android\_alarm\_manager\_plus with a top\-level @pragma callback for background Azan playback even when the app is closed\.

HadithService

Loads and parses the bundled assets/hadiths\.json file; returns a daily\-rotated HadithModel based on the day\-of\-year modulus operation for daily variety\.

HijriService

Uses the hijri\_date package to compute today's Hijri \(Islamic\) calendar date and format it in both English and Urdu for display in the side drawer\.

StreakService

Manages prayer streak data with an in\-memory cache for performance\. Reads from SharedPreferences on first access, then serves from RAM\. Supports legacy format migration, fire\-and\-forget writes, and streak calculations \(current/best\)\.

2\.7 Data Models

The application defines three core data models:

__PrayerTimeModel:__

Holds the five daily prayer times \(Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha\) as String values parsed from the Aladhan API response\. Each time is stored in 24\-hour format \(HH:mm\) for consistent parsing throughout the application\. The model includes a fromJson\(\) factory constructor that extracts prayer times from the API's response structure\.

__HadithModel:__

Represents a single Hadith with fields for: arabic \(original Arabic text\), englishText \(transliteration\), urduText \(Urdu script\), englishTranslation, urduTranslation, englishTafseer \(commentary\), urduTafseer, and reference \(book and hadith number\)\. This model supports the bilingual display of daily Hadiths in the side drawer\.

__DailyPrayerRecord:__

Tracks per\-day prayer completion with: date \(String in "YYYY\-MM\-DD" format\) and five boolean fields \(fajr, dhuhr, asr, maghrib, isha\) indicating whether each prayer was performed\. The model includes toJson\(\) and fromJson\(\) methods for serialization\. All dates are normalized to midnight for consistent map keys in the StreakService cache\.

2\.8 Persistence Layer

All persistent data is stored locally on the device using the SharedPreferences plugin \(key\-value storage\)\. No external database, cloud storage, or user account is required\. This design ensures full offline functionality and respects user privacy\. The persistence strategy uses a two\-tier approach: an in\-memory cache for frequently accessed data like streak records, and SharedPreferences as the durable backing store\.

2\.9 External API Integration

__Aladhan Prayer Times API:__

The application integrates with the Aladhan API \(https://api\.aladhan\.com\) for real\-time prayer time calculation\. This is a free, open API that requires no API key, making it ideal for a community\-focused application\.

__Parameter__

__Description__

Base URL

http://api\.aladhan\.com

Endpoint

GET /v1/timings/\{date\}

latitude

Device GPS latitude \(decimal degrees\)

longitude

Device GPS longitude \(decimal degrees\)

method

2 \(Islamic Society of North America calculation method\)

Response

JSON with data\.timings containing prayer times in 24h format

Timeout

10 seconds

__Overpass API \(OpenStreetMap\):__

The Mosque Map feature uses the Overpass API to query nearby mosques from OpenStreetMap data\. The query searches for nodes tagged as "amenity=place\_of\_worship" with "religion=muslim", as well as "amenity=mosque" and "building=mosque" within a dynamically expanding radius\. The search starts at 3km and progressively expands to 10km, 25km, and 50km until at least 3 mosques are found\.

__Nominatim Geocoding API:__

Used for location search \(forward geocoding\) and reverse geocoding to obtain human\-readable addresses\. Location search includes a 600ms debounce timer to avoid excessive API calls while the user is typing\.

__OSRM Routing API:__

The Open Source Routing Machine \(OSRM\) API at router\.project\-osrm\.org provides walking and driving route calculations between the user's location and selected mosques\. Routes are rendered as polylines on the map with distance and estimated travel time\.

# __3\. Implementation Details \(Code Explanation\)__

This section provides a detailed explanation of the code implementation for each major component of the Awwab application, covering the key classes, algorithms, design patterns, and external dependencies used throughout the codebase\.

3\.1 Application Entry Point \(main\.dart\)

The application's entry point is the main\(\) function in main\.dart, which performs the following initialization sequence:

• Calls WidgetsFlutterBinding\.ensureInitialized\(\) and FlutterNativeSplash\.preserve\(\) to hold the native splash screen during async setup\.

• Initializes the NotificationService, which also initializes AndroidAlarmManager for background alarm scheduling, and creates the notification channels\.

• Reads the saved theme mode from SharedPreferences to restore the user's last theme preference\.

• Wraps the widget tree with MultiProvider, exposing both ThemeNotifier and LanguageProvider to all descendant widgets\.

• Uses Consumer2 to listen to both providers simultaneously, rebuilding the MaterialApp with updated theme and language settings\.

• Configures MaterialApp with AppTheme\.lightTheme and AppTheme\.darkTheme from the centralized theme utility\.

• Sets the SplashScreen as the initial route, which handles the animated transition to the main application\.

The MyApp root widget is implemented as a StatelessWidget since theme and language state are managed externally by providers\. The Consumer2 pattern ensures efficient rebuilds — only the portions of the widget tree that depend on theme or language state are rebuilt when either changes\.

3\.2 Prayer Times — Home Screen \(home\_screen\.dart\)

The HomeScreen is the central hub of the application, implemented as a StatefulWidget spanning approximately 780 lines of code\. It serves as the primary landing screen after the splash animation\.

__Two\-Phase Data Loading Strategy:__

The screen employs a two\-phase loading approach: \(1\) on initialization, it immediately loads cached prayer times from SharedPreferences via PrefsHelper\.getCachedPrayerTimes\(\) for instant display, and \(2\) after a 500ms delay, it fetches fresh prayer times from the Aladhan API using the device's GPS coordinates\. This ensures the user sees prayer times instantly, even before the network request completes\.

__Next Prayer Algorithm:__

The next prayer determination iterates through the five prayers chronologically\. For each prayer, the time string is parsed into a DateTime object using DateTime\.parse\(\)\. The first prayer whose time is after DateTime\.now\(\) is identified as the "next" prayer and highlighted with a distinct visual treatment — a primaryColor border, elevated shadow, and an "Up next" label\. If all five prayers have passed for the day, the method wraps around to tomorrow's Fajr\. A custom \_formatTo12Hour\(\) function converts 24\-hour time strings to 12\-hour AM/PM format for user\-friendly display\.

__Countdown Timer:__

A Timer\.periodic running at 1\-second intervals continuously calculates the remaining Duration to the next prayer and formats it as HH:mm:ss\. The timer auto\-recalculates when the countdown reaches zero, advancing to the next prayer\. The countdown is displayed prominently in a hero card with a gradient background and a custom \_HomeMasjidBackdropPainter that draws a decorative wave\-path mosque silhouette using quadraticBezierTo curves\.

__Side Drawer:__

The home screen features a slide\-out drawer containing: an app branding header; an Islamic Calendar card displaying today's Hijri and Gregorian dates computed by HijriService; a daily Hadith card loaded via HadithService showing Arabic text, English/Urdu translation, Tafseer \(commentary\), and reference — with the Hadith rotating daily based on a day\-of\-year modulus operation; and a quick link to Settings\.

__Notification Integration:__

After fetching fresh prayer times, the home screen calls NotificationService\.scheduleAzanAlarms\(\) to schedule background Azan notifications for all five prayers, and scheduleDailyHadithNotification\(\) to schedule a daily Hadith notification at 8:00 AM\.

3\.3 Qibla Compass Screen \(qibla\_screen\.dart\)

The QiblaScreen provides a real\-time Qibla direction finder using the device's compass sensor and GPS location, implemented in approximately 750\+ lines with custom painting\.

__Qibla Bearing Calculation:__

The Qibla direction is calculated using a Haversine\-based bearing formula\. The app computes the exact angle from the user's current GPS position to the Kaabah coordinates \(21\.4225 degrees N, 39\.8262 degrees E\) using the formula: bearing = atan2\(sin\(deltaLong\) x cos\(kaabaLat\), cos\(userLat\) x sin\(kaabaLat\) \- sin\(userLat\) x cos\(kaabaLat\) x cos\(deltaLong\)\)\. This bearing is combined with the real\-time compass heading from the flutter\_compass plugin to orient the compass needle toward Makkah\.

__Custom Compass Rendering:__

The QiblaCompassPainter \(CustomPainter\) renders a detailed compass rose with cardinal directions \(N, S, E, W\), degree markings at regular intervals, an animated Qibla direction needle, a Kaaba visualization at the Qibla bearing, and alignment indicators\. The rotation is animated smoothly using AnimatedRotation and TweenAnimationBuilder for interpolated transitions\. The screen includes a calibration detection system that monitors compass accuracy and displays a "figure\-8" calibration dialog when low accuracy is detected\.

3\.4 Tasbeeh Counter Screen \(tasbeeh\_screen\.dart\)

The TasbeehScreen is one of the largest screens at approximately 800 lines, implementing a digital prayer bead counter with two tabs managed by a TabController:

__Tab 1 — Dhikr Counter:__

Features a large circular tap button that increments the count on each press\. A custom \_RingPainter \(CustomPainter\) draws a circular progress ring with StrokeCap\.round that fills as the count approaches the target value\. Haptic feedback is triggered on each tap via HapticFeedback\.mediumImpact\(\), and a pulse animation \(ScaleTransition\) plays on the button\. Five preset Dhikr options are presented in a \_DhikrPickerSheet modal bottom sheet: SubhanAllah \(target 33\), Alhamdulillah \(target 33\), AllahuAkbar \(target 34\), Astaghfirullah \(target 100\), and La ilaha illallah \(target 100\)\. Users can also set a custom target through a numeric input dialog\. A congratulatory completion dialog appears when the target is reached\.

__Tab 2 — 99 Names of Allah \(Asma ul Husna\):__

Displays a hardcoded list of all 99 Names of Allah with Arabic text, English transliteration, English meaning, and Urdu meaning\. A live search feature filters the list in real time using case\-insensitive toLowerCase\(\)\.contains\(\) matching across all language fields\. Each name is displayed as a card with large Arabic text in a serif font\. The screen uses glass\-morphism effects on cards with BackdropFilter and ClipRRect\.

3\.5 Azan Reminders Screen \(reminders\_screen\.dart\)

The RemindersScreen \(approximately 600 lines\) manages Azan notification scheduling with a flexible, user\-friendly interface\.

__Manual Reminder System:__

Unlike a simple toggle\-per\-prayer approach, the Reminders screen implements a full manual reminder system\. Reminders are stored as JSON in SharedPreferences under the key "manual\_reminders"\. Adding a reminder follows a two\-step UX: \(1\) a time picker dialog for time selection, and \(2\) a modal bottom sheet \(\_LabelPickerSheet\) for label selection from 9 predefined options \(5 prayers \+ Tahajjud, Du'a, Quran, Custom\) with icons and bilingual English/Urdu labels\. When "Custom" is selected, a TextField appears for free\-text label input\.

__Scheduling and Management:__

Reminders are scheduled via NotificationService\.scheduleManualReminder\(\) with auto\-advance logic \(if the selected time has passed today, the reminder is scheduled for tomorrow\)\. Each reminder receives a unique ID generated from DateTime\.now\(\)\.millisecondsSinceEpoch\. Reminders can be deleted via a confirmation dialog or by swiping with the Dismissible widget \(endToStart direction\)\. A summary strip shows "X Upcoming" and "Y Passed" chip counts\. The FloatingActionButton uses a ScaleTransition with easeOutBack curve\.

3\.6 Streak Tracker Screen \(streak\_tracker\_screen\.dart\)

The StreakTrackerScreen \(approximately 570 lines\) implements a gamified habit tracking system with a GitHub\-style contribution heatmap\.

__Calendar Heatmap:__

The screen uses the table\_calendar package with custom CalendarBuilders\. A \_heatmapColor\(\) function maps prayer completion count \(0\-5\) to opacity levels \(0\.05 to 0\.78\) of the primary color, creating a visual heatmap similar to GitHub's contribution graph\. Days with higher prayer completion appear more saturated\.

__Streak Algorithm:__

Streak calculations are delegated to StreakService\. The current streak algorithm counts backward from today — a day counts toward the streak only if ALL five prayers are marked as completed\. The moment a day with fewer than five completed prayers is encountered, the streak breaks\. The best streak algorithm performs a forward scan through all sorted dates, tracking the longest consecutive run of fully completed days\. Both values are cached in SharedPreferences to avoid recalculation on every load\.

__Daily Prayer Card:__

Selecting a day on the calendar reveals a daily card showing the date, a LinearProgressIndicator with color coding \(green for all 5, orange for 3\-4, primary for 0\-2\), a completion badge \(X/5\), and five toggle rows for each prayer\. Toggling a prayer uses HapticFeedback\.selectionClick\(\) and immediately persists the change\. Entrance animations include FadeTransition on the header \(600ms\) and SlideTransition on cards \(500ms\)\.

3\.7 Prayer Guidance Screen

__Guidance Screen \(guidance\_screen\.dart\):__

The GuidanceScreen serves as a comprehensive Islamic dua and dhikr hub with 10 sections covering: Basic Tasbeeh, Morning & Evening Adhkar, Comprehensive Dhikr, Before & After Salah, Special Situations, Difficult Situations, Firmness of Heart, Depression/Anxiety, Protection, Quranic Duas, and Istikhara\. All content is hardcoded with Arabic text, English/Urdu translations, and Hadith references\. Features include real\-time search across all language fields, expandable accordion\-style sections, and a copy\-to\-clipboard feature for Arabic text\.

__Prayer Guidance Screen \(prayer\_guidance\_screen\.dart\):__

The PrayerGuidanceScreen \(StatelessWidget\) receives a prayerName parameter and displays three main sections: \(1\) a Rakat Breakdown showing counts for Sunnah Muakkadah, Fardh, Sunnah Ghair Muakkadah, and Nafl; \(2\) Step\-by\-Step Instructions with numbered markers; and \(3\) optional Notes on timing and common considerations\. All five prayers are fully covered: Fajr \(4 rakats total\), Dhuhr \(12\), Asr \(8\), Maghrib \(7\), and Isha \(15 including Witr\)\. Complete bilingual English/Urdu content is provided with proper RTL rendering for Urdu text\.

3\.8 Mosque Map Screen \(mosque\_map\_screen\.dart\)

The MosqueMapScreen \(approximately 750 lines\) provides a feature\-rich nearby mosque finder with interactive mapping\.

__Map Engine and Data Sources:__

Built on the flutter\_map package \(OpenStreetMap\-based\) with MapController for programmatic map control\. The screen supports dark mode map tiles \(CartoDB dark tiles\) and standard OSM tiles for light mode\. Mosque data is fetched using a dual API strategy: Nominatim is tried first, then Overpass API as a fallback, ensuring redundancy\.

__Dynamic Radius Search:__

The mosque discovery algorithm progressively expands the search radius \(3km, 10km, 25km, 50km\) until at least 3 mosques are found\. The Overpass query searches for three tag combinations: amenity=place\_of\_worship \+ religion=muslim, amenity=mosque, and building=mosque\. A Set\-based deduplication system using "name\_lat" key patterns filters out duplicate entries\.

__Routing and Navigation:__

The OSRM routing API provides walking and driving routes rendered as polylines on the map\. A travel mode toggle allows switching between foot and car profiles\. Routes are lazily loaded — only the nearest 3 mosques get routes initially, with others loading on selection\. Custom location support allows long\-pressing the map to set a different origin point, with a "Reset to GPS" button to revert\. External navigation launches Google Maps via url\_launcher for turn\-by\-turn directions\.

3\.9 Notification Service \(notification\_service\.dart\)

The NotificationService \(approximately 415 lines\) is implemented as a static utility class with dual notification channels\.

__Dual Channel Architecture:__

Two notification channels are configured: "azan\_channel" uses the system default sound for prayer time banners \(non\-intrusive\), while "reminder\_azan\_channel" uses custom Azan audio \(azan\.mp3\) that auto\-plays when reminders fire\. The channel refresh strategy deletes old channels before recreating them to force Android to pick up sound changes\.

__Background Azan Playback:__

A critical feature is the azanAlarmCallback\(\) function — a top\-level function annotated with @pragma\("vm:entry\-point"\) that is fired by AndroidAlarmManager even when the app is completely closed\. This callback uses AudioPlayer from the audioplayers package to play the Azan audio for 30 seconds\. The alarm is scheduled using AndroidAlarmManager\.oneShotAt\(\) with exact: true, wakeup: true, and rescheduleOnReboot: true flags\.

__Cross\-Platform Support:__

iOS notification support is provided via DarwinNotificationDetails with the Azan sound file\. Timezone handling uses flutter\_timezone to detect the local timezone with a UTC fallback\. Permission handling covers both Android notification permissions and exact alarm permissions\. A daily Hadith notification can be scheduled at a configurable hour with language\-aware content\.

3\.10 Splash Screen \(splash\_screen\.dart\)

The SplashScreen \(approximately 500 lines\) provides a cinematic, multi\-layered animated introduction with three custom CustomPainter classes:

__Animation Architecture:__

Two AnimationControllers drive the animations: a main controller \(2800ms, one\-shot\) drives four staggered Interval animations — bead convergence \(0\-60%\), emblem reveal \(35\-78%\), light wave \(48\-88%\), and background shift \(30\-85%\); and a rotation controller \(14s loop, infinite\) provides continuous bead rotation with a counter\-rotating emblem\.

__Visual Elements:__

PremiumSplashBackdropPainter renders an architectural mosque silhouette with a starfield background\. CinematicSplashPainter animates 33 tasbeeh beads converging from scattered positions \(calculated via sin\(i\*7\.3\) and cos\(i\*3\.7\) offsets\) to a perfect circle using linear interpolation\. EmblemFramePainter draws a rotating Rub el Hizb 8\-point star frame \(two concentric squares rotated by pi/4 with sqrt\(2\) distance scaling\)\. RepaintBoundary widgets isolate painting layers to minimize repaints for performance\. The route transition uses a PageRouteBuilder with FadeTransition \(1100ms\) to cross\-fade into MainWrapper\.

3\.11 Settings Screen \(settings\_screen\.dart\)

The SettingsScreen \(approximately 244 lines\) provides four primary personalization options: \(1\) a Dark Mode toggle that switches the theme via ThemeNotifier\.toggleTheme\(\) from the Provider; \(2\) a Language selector dropdown \(English/Urdu\) that calls LanguageProvider\.setLanguage\(\), instantly updating all UI labels throughout the app; \(3\) an Azan Alerts toggle — when enabled, the screen fetches prayer times \(from cache or fresh via GPS\), cancels any existing notifications, and schedules all five prayers with NotificationService\.scheduleNotification\(\) including the Azan sound; when disabled, all prayer notifications are cancelled; and \(4\) an About dialog using Flutter's built\-in showAboutDialog\(\) with the app description, version, and developer credits\. Error handling shows a Snackbar on failure and resets the switch state\.

# __5\. Challenges and Solutions__

During the development of Awwab, the team encountered several significant technical challenges\. This section documents each challenge and the solution that was implemented\.

5\.1 Accurate Prayer Time Calculation Across Time Zones

__Challenge:__

Calculating accurate prayer times requires precise handling of the user's geographic location and time zone\. Different cities — even within the same country — can have significantly different prayer times, and daylight saving time changes add further complexity\. Additionally, the app needed to display times immediately on launch before the network request could complete\.

__Solution:__

We integrated the Aladhan API, which uses astronomically\-precise calculations based on GPS coordinates with the ISNA \(Islamic Society of North America\) calculation method\. To handle time zones correctly, we used the timezone and flutter\_timezone packages to initialize timezone\-aware TZDateTime objects\. The LocationService wraps the Geolocator plugin with proper permission handling and fallback behavior\. A two\-phase loading strategy was implemented: cached prayer times are loaded instantly from SharedPreferences on launch, while fresh times are fetched from the API after a 500ms delay and the cache is updated\.

5\.2 Reliable Background Notification Scheduling

__Challenge:__

Android's battery optimization \(Doze mode\) aggressively kills background processes and delays AlarmManager alarms\. This made it difficult to ensure Azan notifications fire at the exact scheduled prayer time, especially when the app is closed or the device is idle\. Additionally, the Azan audio needed to play even without user interaction\.

__Solution:__

We implemented a dual notification channel system with background Azan playback\. The android\_alarm\_manager\_plus plugin leverages Android's setExactAndAllowWhileIdle\(\) API for precise alarms during Doze mode\. A top\-level @pragma\("vm:entry\-point"\) callback function \(azanAlarmCallback\) is invoked by the AlarmManager even when the app is completely closed — this callback plays the Azan audio for 30 seconds via AudioPlayer\. The RECEIVE\_BOOT\_COMPLETED permission ensures alarms are rescheduled after device reboot\. The channel refresh strategy deletes and recreates channels to force Android to pick up sound configuration changes\.

5\.3 Real\-Time Qibla Compass Accuracy

__Challenge:__

The device's magnetometer sensor can be inaccurate due to magnetic interference, uncalibrated sensors, or proximity to electronic devices\. This leads to the compass needle pointing in the wrong direction, which is particularly problematic for a prayer direction finder that users rely on for correct prayer orientation\.

__Solution:__

We implemented a calibration detection system that monitors compass accuracy from the flutter\_compass plugin\. When low accuracy is detected, a calibration dialog instructs the user to perform a "figure\-8" motion\. The Qibla bearing is calculated using the Haversine\-based bearing formula relative to the Kaabah coordinates \(21\.4225 N, 39\.8262 E\)\. The compass animation uses AnimatedRotation with interpolation to smooth out noisy sensor data\. The custom QiblaCompassPainter renders a detailed compass rose with degree markings and a Kaaba visualization at the Qibla bearing\.

5\.4 Bilingual Support with RTL Layout

__Challenge:__

Supporting both English \(LTR\) and Urdu \(RTL\) throughout the entire app required careful handling of text alignment, layout direction, and content switching\. Urdu uses Arabic script with right\-to\-left rendering and different typographic requirements\. The switch needed to be instant and affect every screen simultaneously\.

__Solution:__

We implemented a global LanguageProvider using the Provider package with a language code\-based approach\. Every user\-facing string uses a ternary expression checking the isUrdu flag\. The Provider's ChangeNotifier pattern ensures instant, app\-wide updates\. Typography uses Google Fonts with Plus Jakarta Sans for English and Noto Sans Arabic for Arabic/Urdu text, configured through the centralized AppTheme\. All prayer guidance content \(10 dua/dhikr sections, 5 prayer methods, rakat breakdowns\), 99 Names of Allah, navigation labels, reminder labels, and UI strings have complete bilingual versions\.

5\.5 Offline Functionality and Data Persistence

__Challenge:__

The app needed to function effectively without an internet connection while persisting user data like prayer completion streaks, notification preferences, and theme/language settings\. Additionally, frequent reads of streak data during calendar scrolling needed to be performant\.

__Solution:__

We implemented a two\-tier caching strategy: an in\-memory cache in StreakService keeps the full prayer records map in RAM after the first load — all reads hit the cache while only writes go to SharedPreferences disk storage\. "Fire\-and\-forget" writes \(calling setString\(\) without await\) prevent blocking the UI thread\. The Hadith dataset is bundled as a local JSON asset\. Prayer times are cached to SharedPreferences for instant display on launch\. Legacy format migration is handled transparently — if old List\-format data is detected, it is cleared and reset\.

5\.6 Cross\-Platform Compatibility

__Challenge:__

Flutter supports six platforms, but platform\-specific features like notification scheduling, compass sensors, GPS, alarm managers, and map rendering behave differently on each platform\. Android\-specific alarm APIs, iOS background modes, and web PWA configurations all needed separate handling\.

__Solution:__

We used well\-maintained Flutter plugins that abstract platform differences\. Platform\-specific configurations include: AndroidManifest\.xml \(permissions, hardware features, boot receiver\), Info\.plist \(background modes: fetch and remote\-notification, location usage descriptions\), and manifest\.json \(PWA configuration with maskable icons\)\. DarwinNotificationDetails provides iOS\-specific notification configuration\. Map rendering uses flutter\_map with different tile providers for light mode \(OSM\) and dark mode \(CartoDB dark tiles\)\. The android\_alarm\_manager\_plus plugin handles Android's exact alarm scheduling while iOS uses its native notification capabilities\.

5\.7 Performant UI Animations

__Challenge:__

The app features numerous simultaneous animations \(splash screen with 33 animated beads, compass rotation, counter pulse, streak checkmarks, tab transitions\) that need to run smoothly at 60 FPS without jank or excessive battery drain\.

__Solution:__

We leveraged Flutter's GPU\-accelerated animation framework\. The splash screen uses RepaintBoundary widgets to isolate painting layers, minimizing repaints\. Staggered Interval animations within a single AnimationController coordinate multiple visual elements without multiple controllers\. CustomPainter classes render complex visuals \(compass rose, progress ring, beads, star frame\) directly on the Canvas for maximum efficiency\. Implicit animations \(AnimatedContainer, AnimatedOpacity\) handle simple transitions declaratively\. TweenAnimationBuilder provides GPU\-thread animation without manual controller management\.

5\.8 Comprehensive Mosque Discovery

__Challenge:__

Finding nearby mosques required access to a worldwide mosque database\. Commercial map APIs \(Google Maps\) require API keys and incur costs\. Additionally, mosque data completeness varies by region, and the search needed to be robust enough to find results even in areas with sparse data\.

__Solution:__

We implemented a multi\-strategy approach: a dual API fallback system \(Nominatim first, then Overpass\) ensures redundancy\. A dynamic radius search progressively expands from 3km to 50km until at least 3 mosques are found\. Three OpenStreetMap tag combinations are searched simultaneously\. OSRM provides walking/driving route calculations rendered as map polylines\. Lazy route loading \(only nearest 3 initially\) optimizes network usage\. Set\-based deduplication prevents duplicate entries\. Custom location support allows users to search from any map point, not just their GPS position\. All services are completely free with no API keys or usage limits\.
